blocks.text: Living in Campbell Valley, South Langley

parts.t: Campbell Valley is rural South Langley: acreages, hobby farms, horse properties and larger homes around Campbell Valley Regional Park, a short drive from the U.S. border. I grew up on a farm in Langley, so the questions that matter here (ALR status, water, septic, outbuildings and what the land can be used for) are the ones I check first.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 8, 2026, from public sources and my own work in Langley. Rural land rules change, so confirm anything important with the Township and the Agricultural Land Commission.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: ALR and zoning in Campbell Valley

parts.t: On rural land the rules decide what a property is really worth to you, so check them before you fall in love with the barn.
Many Campbell Valley properties are in the Agricultural Land Reserve. Check the ALC map for the exact property.
ALR land is regulated by both the Agricultural Land Commission and the Township. Extra homes, non-farm uses, subdivision and bringing in fill can all need approval, and approval is not guaranteed.

On ALR land the ALC generally allows one principal residence of up to 500 m². On parcels of 40 hectares or less, one additional residence of up to 90 m² may be allowed if the Township’s zoning permits it.
Township zoning sets what buildings and uses are allowed, including animals and outbuildings. Check the zone for the exact address.
Streams and ravines, including along the Little Campbell River, can bring environmental setbacks.
Farm class for property tax is set by BC Assessment and depends on farm income and use, not just on the land being in the ALR.
, and the Township of Langley. Always confirm current rules for the specific property.

blocks.text: Before you buy in Campbell Valley

parts.t: Check the ALC map and ask the Township what the property is zoned and what that allows.
Get a well flow test and a water quality test, and ask for any past results.
Find out the system’s age and service history, and have it inspected.
Ask whether barns, arenas, shops and suites were built with permits.
Look for covenants, rights of way and easements, including any access you rely on.
Ask about farm status and insurance.
Confirm with BC Assessment whether farm class applies, and get insurance quotes for rural property early.
Send me your address and I’ll give you a call to talk about how to get the most value from your home.

Is Campbell Valley in the ALR?
Many properties are. ALR status is set property by property, so check the
for the exact address. You can also check an address with the

Can I keep horses on a Campbell Valley property?
Many properties here are set up for horses, but what is allowed depends on the zone and the land. Check the Township zoning for the exact address, and confirm that barns and arenas were permitted.
Can I build a second home or carriage house?

It depends on ALR status, zoning and lot size. On ALR land the ALC generally allows one principal residence of up to 500 m², and on parcels of 40 hectares or less one additional residence of up to 90 m² if the Township’s zoning permits it. Send me the address and I’ll check before you buy.
Do Campbell Valley homes have wells and septic?
Many rural properties use wells and septic systems. Confirm for each property, and get the water and septic tested before you remove subjects.
The addresses I checked around the park were in the Glenwood Elementary (20785 24 Avenue, K to 7) and Brookswood Secondary catchments. Catchments are set by address, so confirm with the
What is in Campbell Valley Regional Park?

About 33 km of walking trails (about 17 km open to horses), the Campbell Downs equestrian centre with a cross-country course and riding ring, a Nature House, the heritage Annand/Rowlatt Farmstead and Lochiel Schoolhouse, and the paved oval of the former Langley Speedway. Metro Vancouver runs the park.
